The **2018 Vuelta a Castilla y León** was the **33rd edition** of the Spanish cycling stage race, held from **April 20 to April 22, 2018**. Here’s everything I know about the race:

---

### **Overview**
- **Race Category**: 2.1 (UCI Europe Tour)
- **Dates**: April 20–22, 2018
- **Route**: 3 stages covering **490.8 km** in the Castilla y León region of Spain.
- **Winner**: **Rubén Plaza** (Spain, Israel Cycling Academy)
- **Teams**: 18 teams (3 UCI WorldTeams, 8 Pro Continental, 7 Continental)

---

### **Stages**
The race consisted of three stages, all held in Castilla y León:

#### **Stage 1 – Alba de Tormes to Salamanca (187.4 km) – April 20**
- **Winner**: **Carlos Barbero** (Spain, Movistar Team)
- **Key Details**:
  - A hilly stage with a sprint finish.
  - Barbero outsprinted **Jon Aberasturi** (Euskadi–Murias) and **Eduard Prades** (Euskadi–Murias).
  - **Rubén Plaza** took the overall lead after finishing in the top 10.

#### **Stage 2 – Valladolid to Palencia (183.1 km) – April 21**
- **Winner**: **Mihkel Räim** (Estonia, Israel Cycling Academy)
- **Key Details**:
  - A flat stage with a bunch sprint.
  - Räim won ahead of **Jon Aberasturi** and **Enrique Sanz** (Euskadi–Murias).
  - **Rubén Plaza** retained the leader’s jersey.

#### **Stage 3 – Segovia to Ávila (120.3 km) – April 22**
- **Winner**: **Rubén Plaza** (Spain, Israel Cycling Academy)
- **Key Details**:
  - A mountainous stage with a summit finish in **Ávila**.
  - Plaza attacked on the final climb (**Puerto de Navalmoral**) and soloed to victory.
  - He secured the **overall win** by **12 seconds** over **Carlos Barbero** (Movistar).
  - **Eduard Prades** (Euskadi–Murias) finished third overall.

---

### **Final Classifications**
#### **General Classification (GC) – Final Standings**
1. **Rubén Plaza** (Israel Cycling Academy) – **12h 40' 33"**
2. Carlos Barbero (Movistar) – **+12"**
3. Eduard Prades (Euskadi–Murias) – **+16"**
4. Jhonatan Cañaveral (Coldeportes Zenú) – **+22"**
5. Diego Rubio (Burgos BH) – **+26"**

#### **Points Classification**
- **Carlos Barbero** (Movistar)

#### **Mountains Classification**
- **Guillermo Gutiérrez** (Burgos BH)

#### **Young Rider Classification**
- **Jhonatan Cañaveral** (Coldeportes Zenú)

#### **Teams Classification**
- **Euskadi–Murias**

---

### **Key Facts & Highlights**
- **Rubén Plaza** (then 38 years old) won his second **Vuelta a Castilla y León** (first in **2005**).
- **Israel Cycling Academy** (now Israel–Premier Tech) had a strong performance, with Plaza winning the GC and **Mihkel Räim** taking a stage.
- **Movistar** won the opening stage with **Carlos Barbero**, who finished second overall.
- The race was part of the **2018 UCI Europe Tour** and served as preparation for the **Vuelta a España** later in the year.
- The **third stage** was the most decisive, with Plaza’s solo attack securing his victory.

---

### **Teams Participating (18 Teams)**
#### **UCI WorldTeams (3)**
- Movistar Team
- Team Sky (now Ineos Grenadiers)
- LottoNL–Jumbo (now Team Jumbo–Visma)

#### **UCI Professional Continental Teams (8)**
- Burgos BH
- Caja Rural–Seguros RGA
- Euskadi–Murias
- Israel Cycling Academy
- Manzana Postobón Team
- Nippo–Vini Fantini–Europa Ovini
- Rally Cycling
- Team Novo Nordisk

#### **UCI Continental Teams (7)**
- Aviludo–Louletano
- Coldeportes Zenú
- Fundación Euskadi
- Inteja Dominican Cycling Team
- Lokosphinx
- Polartec–Kometa
- W52 / FC Porto

---

### **Notable Riders**
- **Rubén Plaza** (Winner) – A veteran Spanish climber who also won stages in the **Tour de France** and **Vuelta a España**.
- **Carlos Barbero** (2nd overall) – A strong sprinter who later rode for **Dimension Data (now Q36.5)**.
- **Mikel Landa** (Team Sky) – A top GC contender (finished **10th overall**), though he didn’t win a stage.
- **Mihkel Räim** (Stage 2 winner) – An Estonian sprinter who later rode for **Israel–Premier Tech**.

---

### **Broadcast & Media**
- The race was broadcast on **Eurosport** and **Teledeporte (Spain)**.
- Live updates were available on **Cyclingnews** and the **official race website**.

---

### **Aftermath & Significance**
- This was one of **Rubén Plaza’s last major wins** before retiring in **2020**.
- The race was a **key preparation event** for Spanish riders ahead of the **Vuelta a España**.
- **Euskadi–Murias** (a Basque team) had a strong showing, finishing **3rd in the GC and winning the teams classification**.
